demo_input.text: The scientist [MASK] the experiment carefully and recorded the results.

beginner_explanation: BERT reads text in both directions (left-to-right and right-to-left at the same time) and fills in missing words. It's like a fill-in-the-blank test that understands the full context around the blank.
advanced_explanation: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) uses a deep Transformer encoder (12-24 layers) to create contextualized word representations. Pre-training uses Masked Language Modeling (MLM): randomly mask 15% of tokens and predict them using bidirectional context, and Next Sentence Prediction (NSP): predict if sentence B follows sentence A. The input is [CLS] + tokens + [SEP] with segment embeddings and position embeddings. Fine-tuning adds a task-specific head on top of the [CLS] token or token outputs.

formula_cards.title: BERT Input Representation
formula_cards.explanation: BERT combines three embeddings: wordpiece token embeddings, segment (sentence A/B) embeddings, and position embeddings.
formula_cards.example: Input: [CLS] The scientist [MASK] ... → sum of token + segment + position embeddings

formula_cards.title: Masked Language Modeling (MLM) Loss
formula_cards.explanation: Pre-training objective: maximize probability of correct masked tokens given bidirectional context.
formula_cards.example: For 'The scientist [MASK]...', model predicts 'conducted' with P=0.65

formula_cards.title: Self-Attention in BERT
formula_cards.formula: head_i = Attention(XW_i^Q, XW_i^K, XW_i^V); MultiHead = Concat(all heads)W^O
formula_cards.explanation: Each of BERT's 12 layers has 12 attention heads. Each head learns different relationships (syntax, semantics, coreference).
formula_cards.example: Layer 6, Head 8 might focus on subject-verb agreement; Head 3 might track coreference

step_explanations.title: Validate Input with [MASK] Token
step_explanations.description: Check that input text contains [MASK] token for MLM prediction.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: BERT's MLM pre-training requires masked tokens to predict. Without [MASK], it's just encoding.

step_explanations.title: Tokenize with WordPiece & Add Special Tokens
step_explanations.description: Split text into WordPiece subwords, add [CLS] at start, [SEP] between sentences, and convert to token IDs.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: WordPiece handles out-of-vocabulary words by splitting into subwords. Special tokens provide structure.

step_explanations.title: BERT Encoder (12 Layers of Transformer)
step_explanations.description: Pass input through 12 Transformer layers, each with multi-head self-attention and feed-forward networks.
step_explanations.formula: Each layer: MultiHeadAttention → Add&Norm → FeedForward → Add&Norm
step_explanations.why_it_matters: Each layer refines representations by attending to different contextual relationships. Deep layers capture high-level semantics.

step_explanations.title: Predict Masked Token
step_explanations.description: Take the [MASK] position's output, apply the MLM head (linear + softmax), and get top predictions.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: This shows BERT's contextual understanding - it predicts tokens based on full bidirectional context.

hover_annotations.definition: Special token that BERT learns to predict during pre-training. During fine-tuning, it can be used for fill-in-the-blank tasks.
hover_annotations.example: 'The scientist [MASK]...' → BERT predicts 'conducted' with highest probability
hover_annotations.common_mistake: Using [MASK] during inference on tasks it wasn't trained for (it's specifically for MLM pre-training)

hover_annotations.definition: Special token at the start of every BERT input. The final layer's [CLS] output is used for classification tasks.
hover_annotations.formula_meaning: h_{[CLS]}^{final} encodes the entire input sequence for classification
hover_annotations.example: For sentiment analysis, a linear classifier takes h_{[CLS]}^{final} (768-dim) → positive/negative
hover_annotations.common_mistake: Using [CLS] for token-level tasks (use token outputs instead)

references.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
references.authors: Devlin, J., Chang, M.W., Lee, K., and Toutanova, K.
references.relevance: Original BERT paper introducing bidirectional pre-training with MLM and NSP objectives.

references.title: Visualizing and Understanding the BERT Modelf
references.authors: Rogers, A., Kovaleva, O., and Rumshisky, A.
references.relevance: Comprehensive analysis of what BERT learns across its layers and attention heads.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: BERT reads text in both directions and fills in blanks. It understands context from both left and right sides of a word.
receiver_mode_explanations.teaching_notes: Use a simple fill-in-the-blank sentence. Show top predictions with probabilities.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: BERT uses 12-24 Transformer encoder layers with MLM pre-training: randomly mask 15% of tokens and predict them using bidirectional context.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Input: [CLS] + tokens + [SEP]. Representations: Token + Segment + Position embeddings. Output: contextualized embeddings for each token.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: BERT's bidirectional pre-training was a breakthrough, achieving SOTA on 11 NLP tasks. Research shows lower layers capture syntax, upper layers capture semantics. Limitations: fixed input length (512 tokens), compute cost. Led to RoBERTa, ALBERT, ELECTRA improvements.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Limitations: quadratic attention O(n²), not generative (encoder-only). Alternatives: RoBERTa (better pre-training), ALBERT (parameter sharing), ELECTRA (discriminator-based pre-training).

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: BERT-base: 12 layers, 768 hidden, 12 heads, 110M params. Use HuggingFace transformers. Inference: O(L×n²×d) where L=layers, n=seq_len, d=hidden.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Complexity: O(L×n²×d). Memory: O(L×n×d) for activations. API: transformers.AutoModelForMaskedLM, transformers.pipeline('fill-mask').

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: BERT introduced bidirectional pre-training. Show how context from both sides improves predictions vs. left-to-right only.
receiver_mode_explanations.teaching_notes: Quiz: Why is bidirectional better than left-to-right? Exercise: Compare BERT predictions with/without right context. Discuss: Why 15% masking?

research_context: BERT (Devlin et al., 2019) revolutionized NLP by introducing deep bidirectional pre-training. It achieved state-of-the-art on 11 NLP tasks and spawned an entire family of models (RoBERTa, ALBERT, ELECTRA, DeBERTa). Its success demonstrated the power of transfer learning in NLP.

teaching_notes.summary: BERT uses bidirectional Transformer encoders pre-trained with masked language modeling to create contextualized word representations.
quiz_questions: Why is bidirectional context better than left-to-right for understanding 'The scientist [MASK]...'?
What does the [CLS] token represent, and when do we use it?
Why was the 15% masking rate chosen for MLM pre-training?
classroom_demo_tips: Visualize attention weights across layers and heads
Show how predictions change as you add more context
common_misconceptions: BERT understands language (false - it models statistical patterns, not meaning)
BERT can generate text (false - it's encoder-only, not autoregressive)
